sentences.text: Runner beans scrambled up the fence, and tidy rows of vegetables filled the bottom of the garden.
Flowers bloomed in every corner of the secret, walled garden, as though colour had been spilled and left to spread.
Fragrant, blush-pink roses climbed over the trellis by the back door.
Purple flowers tumbled over the wall, a high, crumbling wall that hid the garden from the road.
Weeds choked the flower beds of the neglected, overgrown garden.
The tall, golden sunflowers wilted in the heat, their heavy heads bowed.
Foxgloves nodded in the breeze around the weathered, mossy bench.
Fat, drowsy bees droned among the lavender.
Butterflies flitted from flower to flower in the sunny, sheltered corner by the shed.
A blackbird hopped across the lawn, head cocked, listening for worms.
Grandad was fiercely proud of his immaculate, striped lawn and allowed no football anywhere near it.
A robin sang from the apple tree as the light drained away.
Water trickled from the fountain into the small, shaded pond.
Honeysuckle perfumed the evening air.
Weeds encroached on the path and forced their way between the stones.
A winding gravel path led to the greenhouse.
He dug in the vegetable patch all morning, turning over the damp, dark earth.
She waded into the waist-high stinging nettles in thick gloves and pulled them up by the roots.
The cat basked on the warm stones of the terrace.
The rusting, iron gate swung on its hinges with a long, mournful creak.
Pink and white blossom fluttered to the ground like confetti.
The shadow of the tall, clipped hedge spread across the lawn as the sun went down.
Thick, thorny brambles had all but swallowed the rickety, wooden shed.
Raindrops clung to the delicate, velvety petals like beads of glass.
The storm flattened the borders and snapped the sunflowers at the neck.
The wind tore through the garden, scattering petals and rattling the greenhouse glass.
Nobody had sat in the garden for years, and the swing hung motionless.
The garden hummed with insects and the chatter of sparrows.
It was a tranquil place to sit, with nothing to hear but birdsong and the splash of the fountain.
Something rustled in the nettles at the end of the garden, where the light never quite reached.
